label: Neutral / default — a restrained Roblox UI built to core-platform convention
provenance: Eleven public pages fetched on 2026-09-20: Roblox's own creator documentation, its UI-design curriculum for the shipped Laser Tag sample experience, and two Developer Forum posts written by Roblox staff about the core UI they ship. Every row carries the URL that was actually fetched. Nothing here is recalled from memory and no artwork is stored; each row records what the page states or describes. This genre is unusual in that its subject IS the platform's own UI, so Roblox's documentation of it is a primary source rather than commentary.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/updated-experience-controls-now-live/3215981 — Roblox announcement of the shipped in-experience controls (the topbar every player sees in every experience)
demonstrates: icons are 44 pixels, and the post states the size was chosen to meet WCAG 2.1 target-size guidance at the AAA rating — the platform's own control row is built to an accessibility number, not to a look
the controls are left-aligned and the announcement says the right side is deliberately left for creators, so a well-behaved custom HUD puts its own chrome on the right

two parts only: a hamburger that absorbs everything secondary (report, self view, capture, leaderboard, emotes, inventory, respawn) and a persistent row of live communication toggles (text chat, microphone)
the bar's width is dynamic — it changes as features enable and disable, and on portrait mobile it can span the entire width, so no custom element may assume a fixed gap beside it
two APIs are given for adapting: TopbarSafeInsets to find the reserved space and a signal to react when its width changes
stated intent is consistency and immediate access across every experience, which is what makes this row the neutral baseline other genres decorate around

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/designing-ui-tips-and-best-practices/3074034 — Roblox staff post 'Designing UI - Tips and Best Practices'
demonstrates: the top bar is described as an offset height of 36; a community reply in the same thread updates this to 58 in current clients, so the number is disputed and must be read from the API rather than hardcoded
size and position are to be authored in scale, not offset, with a worked conversion: a 100x100 pixel frame becomes 0.257 scale on both axes

corner radius is to be set in scale (example 0.2) because an offset radius 'appears drastically different between devices' — this is the single construction habit that separates a platform-native panel from a pasted-in one
UIStroke is called out as supporting offset only, never scale, which is why stroke cannot be the load-bearing device in a responsive neutral theme
AnchorPoint conventions are stated plainly: (0,0) top-left, (0.5,0.5) centre, (1,1) bottom-right
ScreenGui.ScreenInsets is given as the mechanism for staying clear of notches, Dynamic Island and core UI
mobile virtual controls occupy the bottom-left and bottom-right corners, and the post's instruction is to design for mobile first and let desktop follow

references.source: https://create.roblox.com/docs/tutorials/curriculums/user-interface-design/implement-designs-in-studio — Roblox's UI curriculum building the HUD of its shipped Laser Tag sample experience, screen by screen
demonstrates: a transparency ladder rather than a palette does the work: layout containers sit at BackgroundTransparency 1 and hold no fill at all, subtle backing sits at 0.15, overlays at 0.3–0.5, and a de-emphasised control at 0.65
corner radius is authored in scale throughout — roughly 0.05 to 0.2 for buttons, 0.075 for a modal container — and some elements deliberately carry no UICorner
UIListLayout padding is expressed in scale as well, 0.025 to 0.035 between horizontal items, with 2–3% margins from the screen edge
one type family across every screen (Montserrat) with weight carrying the hierarchy: Medium for standard, Bold for emphasis, Black reserved for critical alerts
text is pure white on dark surfaces with TextScaled enabled, and no text outline is used anywhere
LayoutOrder is used as z-order intent: headers at -1 so they resolve first, interactive buttons at 2
square elements (crosshair, blast button, icons) hold their shape with UIAspectRatioConstraint rather than with matched width/height values
HUD parts are sized as percentages of the screen — objective frame 50% x 13%, blaster selector 80% x 25%, player display 23% x 8% — so the layout survives any aspect ratio
a pressed state is a swapped PressedImage and a disabled state is a transparency change, not a colour change

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/tutorials/curriculums/user-interface-design/wireframe-your-layouts.md — the wireframing chapter of the same curriculum
demonstrates: screen regions are assigned by category and stay assigned: objective and global state at the top, the action focal point at centre, player state at the sides and periphery

the bottom-left and bottom-right are reserved because the thumbstick and jump button live there; the instruction is to put interactive elements 'near the natural resting position for thumbs' and that reaching away from those corners is 'either uncomfortable or impossible'
one adaptive design is produced for all devices rather than separate mobile and desktop layouts, and the wireframe accounts for Roblox core UI, touch controls and custom elements in the same drawing
balance and symmetry are sought between the custom UI and the system UI — the core UI is treated as part of the composition, not as an obstacle
layouts are tested against a variety of possible backgrounds for legibility, because a translucent neutral UI sits on top of whatever the world is doing

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/tutorials/use-case-tutorials/ui/interactive-ui.md — Roblox's worked build of a settings menu with sliders, given with every property value
demonstrates: the opener is an icon-only gear at top-centre, sized 0.1 in scale but clamped by a UISizeConstraint MaxSize of (inf, 44) — the same 44 the shipped experience controls use, reached independently
the panel is 0.75 x 0.75 in scale, constrained to AspectRatio 2.5, MaxSize 800 wide and MinSize 350 — a neutral panel is a proportion with a pixel ceiling and floor, never a fixed rectangle
the panel is translucent: a dark navy fill at BackgroundTransparency 0.25, so the world stays visible behind it
UICorner on the panel is 0.1 in scale; the slider track and its handle both use 0.5, which UICorner turns into a pill and a circle regardless of dimensions
the slider track carries a UIStroke of thickness 3, black, at transparency 0.25 — the stroke is a soft separation from whatever is behind, not a cartoon outline
close is an icon glyph anchored (1,0) at position (1,-10,0,10) — inset ten pixels INSIDE the panel's top-right corner — at ImageTransparency 0.25, sized 0.15 of the panel with a 1:1 aspect constraint
the accent colour appears exactly twice per control: the handle's stroke and the filled portion of the track; everything else is neutral
opening tweens over 0.5s and closing is instant (0s) with Visible flipped — the exit is not a mirror of the entrance
the gear rotates 45 degrees to signal the open state, so the opener is also the state indicator

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/production/game-design/ui-ux-design.md — Roblox's UI and UX design guidance
demonstrates: prominence is bought with size, negative space, proximity and movement before colour: 'Elements encircled by ample negative space or padding are eye-catching'

'Housing buttons in a container, such as a color surrounding the text or icon, distinguishes them from the background, making them appear interactive' — a bare label is not a button even in a restrained theme
three button states are named as the requirement: hover, depressed, and released (selected)
'Headers and titles containing significant high-level information should be larger and bolder than body text' — the header is a type-scale step, not a separate plaque object
a concrete state convention: when a player cannot afford an item, the price displays in red
icons for related stats share a palette and similar shapes so their function is recognisable as a family
consistency is required across colours, formatting, button placement, icon usage and cost display — the same decision everywhere, which is what 'restrained' actually means here
players choose a PreferredTextSize of Medium (default), Large, Larger or Largest, and the UI is expected to grow with it

elements using TextScaled are NOT scaled by that setting, while AutomaticSize elements grow and TextWrapped elements re-wrap — so honouring the setting is a construction choice made when the label is built
GuiService.PreferredTransparency runs 0 (fully opaque) to 1 (the design's own transparency) and the stated technique is to MULTIPLY each element's BackgroundTransparency by it
GuiService.ReducedMotionEnabled means the player wants motion removed: set TweenInfo.Time to 0, or swap positional movement for a fade
colour may not be the only carrier of meaning — pair it with distinct symbols, the page citing colour blindness in over 5% of the population
sound may not be the only carrier either; in-game events need a visual counterpart

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/ui/size-modifiers.md — Roblox reference for UIScale, UISizeConstraint, UITextSizeConstraint, UIAspectRatioConstraint and AutomaticSize
demonstrates: an explicit floor is stated: 'Do not use MinTextSize property values lower than 9 or the text will be difficult to read'
UITextSizeConstraint is the partner of TextScaled — it holds a scaled label between a minimum and maximum instead of letting it collapse
UISizeConstraint's worked example is MinSize (200,200) with MaxSize (400,400), and the page notes the constraint OVERRIDES a surrounding layout
UIAspectRatioConstraint likewise overrides layout, and is the stated way to keep a thumbnail or icon square
with AutomaticSize on, the Size property becomes a MINIMUM rather than the size — the element grows to its content and respects AnchorPoint while doing it
UIScale multiplies AbsoluteSize and takes children and modifiers such as UIStroke and UICorner with it, which makes it the correct handle for a hover effect

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/ui/appearance-modifiers.md — Roblox reference for UICorner, UIStroke, UIGradient, UIPadding and UIShadow
demonstrates: UICorner Scale rounds by a percentage of the SHORTEST edge, so a value of 0.5 or higher is a pill whatever the element's proportions — this is why a scale radius is safe and an offset radius is not
the four corners are individually addressable (TopLeftRadius, TopRightRadius, BottomRightRadius, BottomLeftRadius), which is how a tab or a docked panel gets its flat edge
UIStroke.ApplyStrokeMode is Contextual for text outlines and Border for the object's bounds, and BorderStrokePosition (Center, Inner, Outer) decides whether a border eats into the shape or grows it
UIStroke transparency is independent of the parent's transparency, so a translucent panel can still hold a crisp edge
UIGradient defaults to Linear, with Offset measured as a percentage of the parent's width or height and TileMode defaulting to Clamp
UIShadow's BlurRadius in scale is relative to the shorter side of the parent, and the page states it does not support text
UIPadding takes UDim values on each side and accepts negative offsets

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/ui/styling/index.md — Roblox's UI styling system (StyleSheet, StyleRule, StyleLink, StyleDerive, tokens, themes, queries)
demonstrates: the documented structure is a chain: a token sheet holding variables as attributes, theme sheets deriving from it and swapping token sets, a design sheet of StyleRules deriving from the theme, and a StyleLink attaching that sheet to a ScreenGui
only one StyleSheet applies per tree, so a coherent neutral UI is one sheet and not a per-element decoration pass

tokens are referenced by a $ prefix, e.g. a single colour token feeding Frame.BackgroundColor3, TextLabel.TextColor3 and UIStroke.Color at once — which is exactly how one restrained palette stays one palette
selectors match by class ('Frame'), by CollectionService tag ('.ButtonPrimary'), by instance name, by nested modifier ('::UICorner') and by GuiState such as Hover
style queries apply rules conditionally on screen size, input type or the player's accessibility settings, so responsiveness is declarable rather than scripted

references.source: https://create.roblox.com/docs/ui/on-screen-containers — Roblox reference for ScreenGui, ScreenInsets and layering
demonstrates: ScreenInsets has four values and CoreUISafeInsets is the DEFAULT — out of the box a ScreenGui already keeps its descendants clear of the top bar buttons and screen cutouts
DeviceSafeInsets covers notches only, TopbarSafeInsets is the dynamic strip inside the top bar row itself, and None opts out of all of it
DisplayOrder layers whole ScreenGuis against one another, higher in front — so a modal is its own container with a higher DisplayOrder, not a high ZIndex inside the HUD
ResetOnSpawn defaults to true, which is why a persistent HUD has to say otherwise explicitly

rules.note: Distilled from the eleven references above. This genre's construction is NOT the simulator's: where the simulator identifies itself with a thick near-black stroke, an overhanging plaque and a red circle hanging off the corner, the neutral theme identifies itself with proportional sizing, translucency, generous padding and a pixel ceiling on every touch target. Numbers below are the ones the sources state; where a value is a range, the sources disagree only in degree and the range is the honest reading.

sizingUnits.rule: author Size and Position in SCALE; use offset only where the engine allows nothing else (UIStroke.Thickness, UIPadding, small nudges like a 10px corner inset)
sizingUnits.clampWith: UISizeConstraint for pixel floors and ceilings, UIAspectRatioConstraint for anything that must stay square
sizingUnits.workedConversion: 100x100 pixels ~= 0.257 scale on both axes at the reference viewport
sizingUnits.why: the staff post gives the conversion and the curriculum sizes every HUD part as a percentage of the screen; a neutral UI is judged on whether it survives a phone and a 21:9 monitor, and fixed pixel rectangles are the thing that fails that test first

cornerRadius.why: the staff post states an offset radius 'appears drastically different between devices' and the reference docs explain that scale measures against the shortest edge, so 0.5 is reliably a pill and a chosen scale keeps the same visual softness on every screen — this single habit is the clearest tell of platform-native construction

targetSize.howToApply: size in scale, then cap with UISizeConstraint MaxSize (inf, 44); treat 44 as the floor on touch as well
targetSize.why: Roblox's shipped experience controls are 44px and the announcement says that number was chosen to hit WCAG 2.1 target size at AAA, and Roblox's own settings-menu tutorial independently caps its opener at MaxSize (inf, 44) — two separate Roblox sources landing on the same number makes it a platform convention rather than a preference

panelSurface.rule: the panel floats over the running world and lets it show through; it is not an opaque sheet and it does not tile a texture
panelSurface.why: the settings tutorial builds exactly this (0.75 scale, AspectRatio 2.5, MaxSize 800, MinSize 350, fill at 0.25) and the wireframing chapter tells you to test legibility against varied backgrounds — translucency is how this genre stays subordinate to the game instead of covering it

transparencyLadder.rule: depth is expressed as steps on this ladder; a container that only arranges children carries no fill at all
transparencyLadder.why: the Laser Tag HUD uses precisely these values and nothing else to separate its layers, which is why that HUD reads as calm — a neutral theme that reaches for a second accent colour where a transparency step would do has already stopped being neutral

panelStroke.rule: a soft separating edge, present so the surface reads against any background — never the identifying feature
panelStroke.why: the settings tutorial's stroke is thickness 3 in black at 0.25 transparency and nothing in these references uses a stroke as decoration; the staff post also notes UIStroke has no scale support, so a heavy stroke authored on desktop becomes a crayon border on a phone

textStroke.instead: white text on a dark translucent surface, with contrast supplied by the surface
textStroke.why: not one of the eleven references applies an outline to text in a neutral UI, and the Laser Tag HUD gets its legibility from pure white on a 0.15–0.25 backing instead — copying the simulator's 2px text stroke into this theme is the single most likely way to make it look wrong

header.rule: the title is text inside the panel, larger and bolder than body text, separated by padding; weight carries it, not a separate object
header.why: Roblox's design guidance says headers 'should be larger and bolder than body text' and the Laser Tag screens set hierarchy with Montserrat Medium/Bold/Black at LayoutOrder -1 — there is no plaque anywhere in this genre, so a generator that reaches for the simulator's overhanging banner produces a costume, not a theme

closeButton.sizeRule: 0.15 of the panel, 1:1 aspect constraint, capped at 44px
closeButton.why: the settings tutorial anchors close at (1,0) and positions it at (1,-10,0,10) with ImageTransparency 0.25 — a quiet glyph inset inside the corner is the neutral form, and the red circle proud of the corner belongs to the cartoon genres and would read as a different product entirely

spacing.rule: group by proximity and separate by empty space; do not draw divider lines between grouped rows
spacing.why: the Laser Tag layouts express every gap in scale (0.025–0.035) with 2–3% screen margins, and Roblox's guidance says elements surrounded by ample negative space are the eye-catching ones — in this genre padding is the emphasis mechanism that colour is in the others

typography.rule: one family, three weights; scale text with TextScaled plus a UITextSizeConstraint, or with AutomaticSize when the player's text-size setting must be honoured
typography.why: the curriculum uses one family and exactly these three weights, the size-modifiers reference states outright not to set MinTextSize below 9, and the accessibility page notes TextScaled elements do NOT respond to PreferredTextSize — so which scaling mechanism is chosen is an accessibility decision, not a styling one

buttonStates.hover: UIScale nudge and/or a GuiState Hover style rule — the modifier scales children and strokes with it
buttonStates.pressed: swap the image or step the fill one rung down the transparency ladder
buttonStates.rule: the control must be housed in a container (fill, border or background) so it reads as pressable at rest
buttonStates.why: Roblox's guidance names hover, depressed and released (selected) as the requirement and states that unaffordable prices display in red; the Laser Tag buttons fade to 0.65 rather than greying out, which keeps a disabled control legible instead of turning it into a smudge

motion.easing: Exponential for chrome, a single overshoot at most for the panel itself
motion.reducedMotion: when GuiService.ReducedMotionEnabled is true, set TweenInfo.Time to 0 or replace movement with a fade
motion.why: the settings tutorial opens over 0.5s and closes instantly, which is the asymmetry that makes a menu feel responsive rather than slow, and the accessibility page gives the exact reduced-motion substitution — motion that cannot be turned off is a defect in this genre

screenRegions.centre: the action focal point (reticle, cast bar, prompt)
screenRegions.topLeft: RESERVED — Roblox experience controls, left-aligned, dynamic width, can span the full width in portrait
screenRegions.topRight: the creator's own chrome, because Roblox states it left that side free
screenRegions.why: the wireframing chapter assigns these categories by region and the experience-controls announcement says the right side was deliberately left to creators; the three reserved corners are not style opinions, they are occupied space, and UI placed there is unreachable on a phone

safeArea.screenInsets: CoreUISafeInsets (the ScreenGui default) for ordinary UI; TopbarSafeInsets only for something that must live in the top bar row
safeArea.topbarHeightPx: read it at runtime from GuiService.TopbarInset or GuiService:GetInsetArea — do not hardcode
safeArea.topbarHeightDisputed: the staff post says an offset height of 36; a reply in the same thread says 58 in current clients
safeArea.reactToWidth: subscribe to the width-change signal, because the controls resize as features toggle
safeArea.why: two Roblox sources give two different top bar heights, which is the argument for reading the inset rather than trusting either number, and the default ScreenInsets already solves the common case — most 'my UI is behind the topbar' construction is undone by leaving the default alone

layering.rule: each modal or overlay is its own ScreenGui with a higher DisplayOrder; ZIndex and LayoutOrder order things WITHIN one container
layering.resetOnSpawn: set false explicitly on any persistent HUD
layering.why: the containers reference states DisplayOrder layers whole ScreenGuis and that ResetOnSpawn defaults to true — a HUD that vanishes on respawn is the classic symptom of neither being set

iconography.rule: square, held by UIAspectRatioConstraint, ScaleType Fit, authored white so a Color3 can tint them; icons in one stat family share palette and silhouette
iconography.never: an icon carrying meaning that no symbol or label repeats
iconography.why: the curriculum constrains every icon to 1:1 and uses white source art for runtime tinting, and the accessibility page requires symbols alongside colour because colour alone excludes over 5% of players

grid.rule: a neutral list is full-width rows with an icon at the left, a label block, and the value or action at the right; when a grid is genuinely needed it is 3 across with square tiles, not 4
grid.why: the neutral theme's own row in ui-kit-themes.ts declares layout 'rows', and nothing in these references packs dense tile walls the way the simulator sources do — restraint here means fewer, wider, more legible rows

themeSystem.rule: emit one token StyleSheet (colour, radius, spacing, type), a theme sheet deriving from it, a design sheet of StyleRules, and a single StyleLink on the ScreenGui
themeSystem.selectors: class, .Tag, instance name, ::UICorner modifier, GuiState (Hover), @Query for screen size / input / accessibility
themeSystem.why: the styling docs state only one StyleSheet applies per tree and that a token referenced as $Name can feed BackgroundColor3, TextColor3 and UIStroke.Color at once — a restrained theme survives only if its restraint is declared in one place rather than repeated per element, which is also what makes it re-themeable later

explicitlyNotThis: NOT a 3–4px near-black stroke on every panel, card and button — this genre's edge is 1–3px at 0.25 transparency, or absent
NOT an overhanging title plaque with its own stroke — the title is a type step inside the panel
NOT a red circle close button proud of the top-right corner — close is a quiet glyph inset 10px inside it
NOT text with an outline — contrast comes from a dark translucent surface under white text
NOT a gradient bevel on buttons — the pressable read comes from the container plus a hover and pressed state
NOT fixed pixel card heights — proportions with a UISizeConstraint ceiling and floor
NOT 4-across tile walls — rows, or 3 across at most

These seven are the simulator genre's identifying construction, recorded here as the boundary because the two files sit in the same folder and a generator that blends them produces a cartoon frame around neutral content, which is the near-miss this library exists to stop.

shippedThemeReadNotRendered.how: READ from apps/worker/src/ui-kit-themes.ts. NOT rendered in Studio and NOT compared by eye. This section is a source reading, not an observation of pixels, and must not be cited as one.
shippedThemeReadNotRendered.themeRowDeclares: id 'studio', label 'Neutral', layout 'rows', radius 16, stroke 1, titleSize 28, cardHeight 144, hudSide 'right', outline '#05080b', panel '#141a20', card '#202933'
agreements: hudSide 'right' matches Roblox reserving the right side of the topbar row for creators
layout 'rows' matches this genre's row-first convention
stroke 1 is already inside the 1–3px range these references support, unlike the simulator's 4
unresolvedAgainstTheseRules: radius 16 is an OFFSET pixel value; every source here authors radius in scale, so the same theme will read differently on a phone than on a monitor
cardHeight 144 is a fixed pixel height where these references use proportion plus a UISizeConstraint
outline '#05080b' is a near-black cartoon outline colour on a theme whose references call for a soft translucent separating edge
the theme row carries no transparency value at all, and the transparency ladder is the primary depth mechanism in every reference here
no target-size ceiling exists in the theme row, so nothing enforces the 44px convention both Roblox sources land on
shippedThemeReadNotRendered.note: These five are candidates for a CLOSED/OPEN ledger of the kind simulator.json carries, but that ledger is earned by rendering the theme and looking at it. Until someone does that, this stays a reading of source and is labelled as one.

honestLimits: All eleven references are Roblox's own documentation and Roblox staff posts about the core UI the platform ships. For this genre that is a primary source — the subject IS the platform's default — but it is not the same evidence as measuring five independent shipped games, and it should not be described as if it were.

No screenshots were examined. Every number here is quoted from a page that was fetched, not read off an image, so there are no proportional approximations in this file and also no measurements of a real game's panel.
The top bar height is genuinely disputed between two statements in the same thread (36 and 58); the rule records the disagreement and says to read the inset at runtime rather than picking a winner.

This genre has not been rendered in Studio and compared by eye. simulator.json earned its ledger that way and found a defect invisible in source; until the same is done here, shippedThemeReadNotRendered is deliberately not written in the CLOSED/OPEN vocabulary.
